Q1. What is “BEDIS,” and why do I need it?
A. BEDIS is the Gilgen keypad/program switch. It lets you set Manual, Hold-Open, Automatic, Partial-Open, Exit-Only, and Night, run a Reset/teach-in, and read error codes without a laptop—speeding commissioning and reducing callbacks.

Q2. How does the SLM’s “self-learning” protect safety and reliability?
A. After a Reset, the controller measures friction and door mass, automatically sets end-positions, and caps speed/force to a safe envelope—typically ~0.6–0.7 m/s opening speed and 150 N maximum static force.

Q3. Is the SLM suitable for large or heavy doors?
A. Yes. Published envelopes document 1 × 160 kg (single leaf) and 2 × 130 kg (bi-parting), with SLM-DUAL options for heavier assemblies. Telescopic 2- and 4-leaf configurations are also supported.

Q4. What happens during a power failure?
A. With the battery pack fitted, the SLM can maintain standard operation for up to ~30 minutes, preserving access/egress and site security.

Q5. Can the SLM integrate with locks and nightly security modes?
A. Yes. The electromagnetic lock integrates with Night and Exit-Only selections on BEDIS
column2: the controller monitors lock status during setup and operation.

A. The running gear uses ball-bearing rollers with a wear-resistant synthetic tread and decoupled carrier profiles to suppress vibration and rail scuffing—one reason SLM installations are known for low acoustic signatures.

Q7. Is this kit compatible with my existing sensors and profiles?
A. In most professional retrofits, yes. The SLM accepts standard activators/safety sensors via the controller and BEDIS bus, and offers multiple mounting methods (between jambs, lintel, wall) and profile options
column2: verify on site for legacy combinations.

The result is motion that feels confident and consistent through seasons, pressure differentials, and traffic spikes.

Inspect Motor output (Pins 43-44) and Incremental encoder ribbon cable seating.

column1: Is this the correct replacement motor for Dorma ES200 automatic door?

If your current motor label displays GR 63×55 30V or your system documentation specifies these parameters, Dunkermotoren GR63x55 Motor is a direct replacement. The assembly includes the exact SG80K gearbox and RE20S encoder used in original ES200 installations, ensuring perfect compatibility. We recommend checking your motor nameplate or contacting our technical team with your system details for verification.
What's the difference between Dunkermotoren motor and cheaper alternatives?

The Dunkermotoren GR 63x55 from Doordynamic offers superior longevity with 3-5 times longer service life, smoother operation through ultra-low cogging torque technology, and better energy efficiency. The premium ball bearings, Class F insulation, and precision manufacturing result in consistent performance over millions of cycles. While generic motors may cost 30-40% less initially, they typically require replacement every 1-2 years in commercial applications, making genuine Dunkermotoren motor more economical long-term when factoring in replacement costs, labor, and downtime.
Why does my motor say ""Made in China"" when Dunkermotoren is a German company?

Dunkermotoren operates manufacturing facilities in both Germany (Bonndorf) and China (Taicang) to serve global markets efficiently. The China facility produces motors under identical quality standards, ISO certifications, and quality control procedures as their German production. All manufacturing follows the same technical drawings, uses the same grade materials, and undergoes the same testing protocols. The production location is chosen based on logistics and market proximity, not quality considerations.
Can I use a 30V motor if my system operates at 24V?

Voltage specifications must match your controller output exactly. Using a 30V motor on a 24V system will result in approximately 20% reduced torque and speed, potentially causing door malfunction, especially with heavier door panels. The motor may struggle to overcome starting friction and could overheat from drawing excessive current. Doordynamic stocks 24V variants of the GR63x55 motor - contact our technical team to ensure you receive the correct voltage variant for your specific system.

While the motor features plug-and-play connectivity for straightforward installation, Doordynamic recommends professional installation to ensure proper alignment, electrical connections, and system programming. Professional installation ensures correct mounting alignment to prevent premature wear, proper electrical connections to avoid damage to motor or controller, accurate encoder calibration for smooth operation, and optimal parameter programming for your specific door configuration. Professional installation also preserves your warranty coverage and often includes initial system optimization.
How does the motor perform in extreme weather conditions?

The standard GR63x55 operates reliably from -20°C to +60°C, covering most commercial environments. For extreme conditions, specialized variants are available. The motor's robust design includes thermal protection to prevent overheating, sealed bearings that resist moisture ingress, and materials selected for thermal stability. In cold conditions, the motor maintains sufficient starting torque even at -20°C, while in hot environments, the Class F insulation provides substantial thermal margin for continuous operation.
Can this motor be used with door systems other than ES200?

While optimized for ES200 systems, the Dunkermotoren GR 63x55 can potentially work with other automatic door controllers that match its electrical specifications. However, compatibility depends on voltage requirements, control signal compatibility, encoder feedback interpretation, and mounting interface dimensions. Doordynamic recommends consulting our technical team before attempting installation in non-ES200 systems to ensure compatibility and optimal performance.

The motor requires minimal maintenance thanks to its sealed ball bearing design and robust construction. Recommended maintenance includes quarterly visual inspection for unusual wear or damage, annual cleaning of the encoder disc with compressed air, annual lubrication of the gearbox with specified gear oil, and carbon brush inspection every 2,000 hours of operation. This simple maintenance schedule ensures optimal performance throughout the motor's service life and can often extend operational life beyond typical expectations.

At the heart of Dunker's motor assembly lies decades of German engineering expertise. The GR63x55 brushed DC motor combines cutting-edge design principles with robust construction standards, resulting in a powerhouse that consistently outperforms conventional sliding door motors in both longevity and operational efficiency. With its nominal power rating of 100 watts and impressive 3350 RPM speed capability, gr63x55 dunkermotoren effortlessly handles door panels weighing up to 200 kg in single configurations or 160 kg per panel in bi-parting setups. The primary Dunkermotoren GR 63x55 motor unit provides the raw power, while the precision-machined SG80K worm gearbox delivers optimal torque conversion with its carefully calibrated 15:1 gear ratio. The RE20S encoder ensures precise position feedback, enabling smooth acceleration curves and gentle deceleration patterns that protect both the door mechanism and building structure from unnecessary stress.

One of the defining characteristics that sets the dorma motor apart from competitors is its exceptionally low cogging torque design. Cogging torque, the unwanted jerky movement that occurs when permanent magnets interact with the motor's slots, has been virtually eliminated in the GR series through sophisticated engineering. This achievement means your automatic doors operate with the smoothness of high-end elevator systems, creating a premium impression for every visitor. Dunkermotoren's engineering team has spent decades perfecting this technology. Through careful optimization of the motor's physical structure, magnetic material selection, and precise manufacturing tolerances, they've achieved cogging torque levels that minimize mechanical vibrations throughout the entire drive system. This reduction in vibration not only enhances the user experience but also significantly extends the life of connected components such as gearboxes, bearings, and door tracks. The low cogging torque design also contributes to the motor's exceptional energy efficiency. Without the constant fight against magnetic resistance, the GR63x55 requires less power to maintain smooth operation, reducing your facility's energy consumption and operational costs over the motor's extended service life.

What truly distinguishes Dunker's motor from budget alternatives is its exceptional performance envelope. Operating at 30 volts DC, the motor maintains consistent power delivery across varying load conditions, ensuring reliable operation whether your doors experience light pedestrian traffic or continuous heavy commercial use.
Brushed DC Technology: The Smart Choice for Door Automation

While brushless motors receive significant attention in the motor industry, Dunkermotoren's advanced brushed DC technology in the GR63x55 offers distinct advantages for automatic door applications. The brushed design provides exceptional starting torque, crucial for overcoming the static friction of heavy door panels. This high starting torque ensures reliable operation even when doors have accumulated dust, debris, or minor mechanical resistance over time. The simplicity of brushed motor control translates directly into system reliability. Unlike brushless motors that require complex electronic commutation, the Dunkermotoren GR 63x55 operates with straightforward voltage regulation. This simplicity means fewer potential failure points in your control system and easier troubleshooting should service ever be required. When combined with modern incremental encoders, these motors deliver position and speed control that matches or exceeds brushless alternatives at a fraction of the complexity. Furthermore, the carbon brush technology in Dunkermotoren GR63x55 Motors have been refined to deliver exceptional service life. Through the use of premium brush materials and optimized commutator design, typical service intervals extend well beyond 5,000 operational hours in commercial door applications, often reaching 8,000 hours or more with proper maintenance.

Every Dunkermotoren GR 63x55 motor that Doordynamic supplies undergoes rigorous quality control testing before leaving the production facility. The manufacturing process adheres to strict ISO 9001:2015 certification standards, ensuring consistent quality whether produced in the original Bonndorf facility in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, or at Dunkermotoren's state-of-the-art Taicang facility in China. The motor's rugged construction features premium-grade neodymium-free magnetic materials that resist demagnetization even under extreme operating conditions. This design choice not only ensures consistent performance throughout the motor's life but also demonstrates Dunkermotoren's commitment to sustainable manufacturing by avoiding rare earth materials. The armature winding utilizes Class F insulation, rated for continuous operation at temperatures up to 155°C, providing exceptional thermal margin for even the most demanding applications. Field data from thousands of installations worldwide demonstrates that Dunkermotoren GR63x55 Motors typically achieve three to five times the operational lifespan of budget replacements. Commercial facilities report average service intervals exceeding 1 million cycles when properly maintained, with many installations surpassing 2 million cycles in moderate-use environments. This remarkable durability translates directly into reduced maintenance costs, minimal downtime, and exceptional return on investment.

The GR63x55 motor incorporates design features that address the real-world challenges of commercial door operation. The motor's low moment of inertia enables rapid acceleration and deceleration, critical for maintaining traffic flow during peak periods. This responsive performance ensures doors open quickly when sensors detect approaching pedestrians, then close promptly to maintain building climate control. The integrated ball bearing system at the motor output shaft handles both radial and axial loads with exceptional durability. This robust bearing configuration has been tested to withstand the continuous stress of commercial operation, including the periodic impact loads that occur when doors reach their travel limits. The sealed bearing design prevents contamination from dust and moisture, ensuring consistent performance even in challenging environments. Additionally, the motor's electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) design meets stringent EN 61000-6-2/3 standards, ensuring it won't interfere with sensitive electronic equipment in hospitals, data centers, or modern office buildings. This low electromagnetic interference (EMI) characteristic makes the Dunker motor ideal for installations in medical facilities where electronic interference could affect critical equipment.

Designed specifically for ES200 automatic door systems, dorma motor ensures perfect compatibility with existing control architectures. The integrated RE20S encoder provides high-resolution position feedback compatible with all standard ES200 microprocessor controllers, including both older legacy systems and the latest digital control units. This universal compatibility ensures that whether you're maintaining a system installed a decade ago or commissioning a brand-new installation, the Dunkermotoren GR 63x55 will integrate seamlessly. Premium Dorma Track Wheels: ES200 Carriage Wheel Assembly

Looking for reliable dorma track wheels? The Dorma ES200 carriages, hang wheels, sliding door trolleys or door connections, are precision-engineered components fixed on door panels or door wings as connections to the track rail profile. For frameless sliding glass doors or french doors, a glass clamp is required to joint the glass panel and trolleys. (This carriage is fully compatible with the Dorma ES200 system).
Typically, there are 4 pieces of carriage in a standard pack of Dorma ES200, each moving wing of the door needs 2 pcs.
• Bi-parting sliding doors or double sliding doors – 4 pcs (left x 2pcs, right x 2pcs)
• Single sliding doors – 2 pcs (left x 1pc, right x 1pc)
Model / Part Name: Dorma ES200 / ES200e Carriage Wheel Assembly (also known as Dorma Carrier, ES200 Carriers, Carriage/Hang Wheel).
System Compatibility: Designed for the Dorma ES200 operator family
column2: widely used on ""Standard"", 2D, and EASY/ES200e variants.

column1: Function: Precision trolley that links each sliding door leaf to the track rail. Functioning as high-performance dorma track wheels, the assembly uses two load-bearing dorma rollers plus a smaller anti-riser (anti-jump) guide wheel and provides height/level adjustment via an eccentric wheel.
Quantity per Door: Two carriers per moving leaf (left + right). A bi-parting entrance uses four carriers total.
• Dorma ES200 Standard: up to 1 x 200 kg or 2 × 160 kg.
Door Types: Compatible with framed aluminum leaves or frameless glass when paired with the appropriate glass clamp between glass and trolley.
Typical Kit: Left and right carriers supplied
column2: standard Dorma ES200 sets use 4 pcs for two-leaf doors.

column1: The Carriage Wheel Assembly, often called the Dorma Carrier, is the precision trolley responsible for suspending each door leaf on the Dorma ES200 track and delivering smooth, quiet travel in demanding commercial environments. In every opening, these heavy-duty dorma track wheels do the heavy lifting: they bear the door load, maintain alignment with an anti-riser guide wheel, and provide millimetric height adjustment through an eccentric mechanism to fine-tune clearances and sightlines.

Dorma ES200 is one of the most widely deployed automatic sliding door platforms, supported across standard, escape-route, and cost-optimized variants. This carrier assembly is designed for fitting rails and door connections perfectly. In practice, that means straightforward hang-and-adjust service calls whether you’re replacing worn dorma rollers in a retail storefront or re-commissioning a hospital corridor entrance after glazing work.

The correct Carriage Wheel Assembly is essential for meeting the operator’s certified weight limits and duty cycle. Matching carriers to the operator class keeps the rolling resistance low, reduces rail wear, and preserves stop-to-stop travel accuracy—especially important for Partial Open and Night/Bank modes where repeatable positioning is critical.

Each Dorma ES200 Carrier pairs two primary dorma rollers with an anti-rise guide wheel. The anti-riser prevents uplift under transient loads (like wind gusts or an off-center push). The eccentric on the main dorma roller axis offers predictable, repeatable height adjustment so you can set reveals, minimize mullion clash, and achieve silent travel along the profile.

Ecosystem Continuity: Dorma ES200 has been the backbone of countless storefront and institutional entrances for years. Using a carrier matched to the OEM geometry (Part Number 9925518001150) protects the investment in rails, end stops, and safety peripherals while ensuring parts availability worldwide.

Compliance Ready: These platforms are engineered to the European DIN 18650 and EN 16005 safety frameworks for automatic doors. A properly adjusted carrier helps the operator achieve the monitored forces and edge safeguarding those standards expect.
Pre-load check: Before hanging, roll each carrier by hand

Q1. Is this set of dorma track wheels fully compatible with Dorma ES200 / EASY?
A. Yes. This carrier style is built for Dorma ES200 family rails and door connections and is commonly specified for Standard, 2D, and EASY installations.
Q2. How many Dorma ES200 Carriers do I need per door?
A. Use two per moving leaf (one left, one right). Bi-parting doors therefore require four carriers total.
Q3. What does the small middle wheel do?

A. That is the anti-riser guide wheel. Together with the carrier’s eccentric wheel, it lets you level the leaf and prevents uplift. After adjustment, the anti-riser should not contact the top track along the travel path.
Q4. What door weights does this support?
A. Follow the operator’s certified limits: Dorma ES200 up to 1 x 200 kg or 2 × 160 kg

column1: Q5. I’m hanging frameless glass. Do I need anything else?
A. Yes—use rated glass clamps between each glass leaf and trolley to join the panel to the rail profile safely.
Q6. How do I level the door after hanging it on the Carriage Wheel Assembly?
A. Adjust height/level via the eccentric dorma roller wheel and set the anti-riser so it clears the rail at all positions. Then securely tighten the lock-nuts.

Premium Electro Mechanical Lock for Sliding Doors

Upgrade the security and efficiency of your facility with the industry-leading electro mechanical lock. Specifically engineered for the Dorma ES200 automatic sliding door opener, this multifunctional locking device combines the return pulley, belt tensioning, and an advanced electric lock mechanism into one compact module. By integrating a mechanical lock electrical solution directly inside the header, it provides seamless fail-secure operation without the visual clutter of external maglocks.

Whether you are upgrading a standard entrance or needing a reliable alternative to an es200 electric strike, our electro mechanical locks deliver quiet, robust performance. This electro lock is the ultimate component for maintaining the integrity and security of any dorma sliding door lock system.
For engineers and installers, verifying the correct parts is critical. Below are the precise technical details for this locking module:
Core Function: Electronically controlled mechanical blocking integrated with belt tensioner and pulley.
Lock Behavior: Fail-secure (remains physically locked when power is off
System Compatibility: Perfectly fits the ES200 and ES200 EASY platforms.
Controller Integration: Seamlessly interfaces with Basic Module (BM) and Function Module (FM) architecture.
Standards Compliance: Supports EN 16005 / DIN 18650 requirements when installed correctly with approved safety sensors.
Why Choose This Integrated Electric Lock Mechanism?

When staff or customers tug on a closed sliding entrance, you need a locking solution that holds with unwavering confidence. Our electro mechanical lock does exactly that for ES200 operators. Instead of surface-mounting vulnerable magnetic locks, this unit mechanically blocks the drive on the exact axis of motion.
From a facility manager's perspective, this integrated approach offers several practical benefits:
Cleaner Architecture: Eliminates separate standalone idlers, keeping the glass and header clean and tampering points to an absolute minimum.
Fail-Secure Dependability: Meet demanding retail and healthcare security policies. In a power outage, the door stays dependably locked until power and access commands are restored.
Predictable Commissioning: The ES200 controller dictates the timing of the lock release versus the motor start, preventing shuddering and ensuring smooth opening cycles.
Simplified Servicing: Replacing part 9925520101150 tackles the lock, pulley, and tensioner all at once, leading to faster installs and shorter service calls.

Q1. Is this the right lock for my ES200?
A. Yes. This is the exact electro mechanical lock specified for those headers. It is managed directly by the controller during opening and closing cycles.

Q2. Can I use it on an ES200 EASY door?
A. Absolutely. The ES200 EASY shares the same component architecture, making this replacement lock (4000105) compatible in the vast majority of cases.

Q3. How does this differ from an external maglock or typical es200 electric strike?
A. Unlike magnetic locks that attach to the leaf or frame, this electric lock mechanism sits completely hidden inside the header. It mechanically blocks the belt drive rather than relying purely on magnetic holding force, yielding a cleaner look and precise operational alignment.

Q4. How does the mechanical lock electrical integration perform during power loss?
A. It is designed to be fail-secure. The lock safely secures the drive when power is cut. Once power returns alongside an authorized open command, it immediately releases.

Q5. Do I still need a separate tensioner?
A. No. Because this module ingeniously incorporates the idler/pulley and belt tensioning, it completely replaces those standalone components.

Terminal 2 (LED): LED status indicator for operation and faults.
Terminal 3 (Start): Start pushbutton for manual operation testing.

[ + ] UP pushbutton: For increasing the parameter or value indicated.
[ - ] DOWN pushbutton: For decreasing the parameter or value indicated.
SERV. (Service): Pushbutton for performing the functions of the service pushbutton.
Display Overview: Features critical parameters such as P. (Program mode), 0. (Opening speed), C. (Closing speed), and d. (Hold open time).

Ensure your automatic sliding doors operate at peak efficiency with the authentic gilgen door systems control panel. Widely recognized in the industry as the Bedis switch pad or electronic remote control, this highly reliable interface is the standard control unit designed seamlessly for Gilgen SLM series drive systems.
OEM Quality: Genuine replacement part designed specifically for Gilgen automatic door operators.
Full Control: Acts as the primary mode selector, allowing you to easily switch between operating modes (Automatic, Open, Closed, Night, Exit Only).
Durable Interface: The robust membrane keypad is built to withstand high-traffic industrial and commercial environments.
Easy Installation: Plug-and-play compatibility with your existing control setups.

This Bedis program switch is critical for the daily management of your entrance system. If your current selector is unresponsive or has a cracked faceplate, immediate replacement is recommended to maintain building security.
Part Type: Electronic Remote Control / Digital Program Switch

column2: Interface: Diagnostic LEDs with membrane push buttons

column1: Mounting: Fits into any standard plug socket (supports surface or concealed mounting)
For proper installation and operation, always refer to the official gilgen bedis manual. The BEDIS unit features a patented data transmission design meant for precise control and easy diagnostics.
System Architecture: Utilizes a highly stable two-wire bus system for data transmission.
Functionality: Provides access to a wide choice of options for the selection of door programs, adjustment of running functions, and a built-in self-diagnostic display.
Documentation: Looking for the full programming guide? You can access the bedis handleiding (manual) for complete configuration steps.
When connecting the operator, strictly follow the technical specifications outlined in the bedis wiring diagram to avoid signal loss or control failure.
Required Cable Type: The connection must use a shielded cable (specifically U72M or DIN 47100 CY).
Maximum Distance: Using the specified shielded cable guarantees reliable functioning and data transmission up to a distance of 50 meters (50 m).
Port Setup: Simplified two-wire connection minimizing installation complexity.

When your sliding door stops working, the BEDIS unit provides a visual self-diagnostic display to help identify gilgen door error codes. Below is the breakdown of the diagnostic LED panel used for troubleshooting:
Indicates an active fault. You must read the numbered LEDs to identify the specific error.
Indicates the system requires a hard reset. You can perform a gilgen slm reset by pressing the designated reset button to clear transient faults.
Relates to opening (Vs) or closing (Vc) speed settings. Recalibrate if the door stutters.
Specific sensor, motor, or lock faults. Check surrounding hardware based on the specific binary combination.

If you have checked the wiring, continuously face the red ERROR LED, and the reset steps cannot eliminate the fault, it usually indicates that the internal electronic components of the control unit have suffered irreversible damage (e.g., from a power surge). In this case, we highly recommend purchasing a brand-new, genuine replacement part to restore your Gilgen SLM door's automatic operation immediately.

End Stop/Door Buffer For SL190 Automatic Sliding Doors

A pair of end stops, door limits, door stops or end buffers are fixed on both side of automatic sliding door rail, they provide a buffer and space limiting to automatic door opening. The smart SL190 automatic sliding door controller will detect and record the position of these stoppers when running the automatic learning cycle or commissioning, position information is written to SL190 control memory as automatic running parameters.

When the rubber stick on the end stop is found damaged, corrosive or missing, it’s recommend that a new end stop or rubber be replaced immediately. Otherwise door’s glass panels could be cracked when hitting the edge without buffers.
Remark: Please rerun the commissioning procedure after new end stop/buffer is installed.

● 2 pieces (1 pair) included in SL190 opener kit set

Q1. What does “dual technology” mean on IXIO-DT1?
A. It blends microwave Doppler (to open the door for approaching traffic) with active infrared presence (to protect stationary or slow-moving users in the threshold). The fusion cuts nuisance opens while keeping the close zone safe.

Q2. How high should I mount the sensor?
A. For pedestrian doors, the recommended range is 6’6″ to 11’6″. Select height by header geometry and required curtain footprint

Q3. How do the “visible spots” help?
A. They project red alignment points onto the floor so you can see the IR curtain edges in real time. Pair this with the angle/width/tilt adjustments to paint the exact safety area you want.

Q4. Does IXIO-DT1 support energy-saving setups?
A. Yes. Use unidirectional radar logic (ignore receding traffic) and appropriate IR immunity to reduce false activations—lowering air-loss while preserving safety.

Q5. Is it compliant with modern door safety practices?
A. The sensor is internally monitored and supports external monitoring from the controller. When installed and tested with compliant safety devices, it aligns with ANSI/BHMA A156.10 practices and EN 16005 design methodology.

Q6. What outputs are available for my controller?
A. Two independent outputs (one electromechanical and one solid-state relay) plus a test input for monitored installations. That architecture plays well with contemporary controllers and documented commissioning.

Q7. Does IXIO-DT1 work on side-lites or curved doors?
A. Yes. The base unit covers single and bi-parting doors

Q8. What should technicians do after installation?
A. Run a full learn/functional test: adjust angle/width, verify spot-based alignment, set microwave sensitivity and IR immunity, then perform monitored test cycles with the controller before hand-off.

The IXIO-DT1 is BEA’s benchmark dual-technology sensor for premium pedestrian sliding doors. It pairs a 24.150 GHz microwave channel for approach detection with two dense IR presence curtains, delivering reliable activation and meticulous threshold safety in one compact, IP54-rated unit. For facility teams who manage flagship retail, healthcare corridors, airports, or campuses, bea ixio dt1 offers the rare mix of fast commissioning, energy-aware logic, and monitored safety that keeps entrances responsive and compliant day after day.

High-resolution safety where it matters most. Many sensors “see” motion but miss stationary feet, mobility aids, or a cart that pauses at the sill. IXIO-DT1’s two IR curtains each render up to 24 detection spots, creating a tight grid that catches static presence right where contact risk is highest. With visible alignment spots, technicians can instantly verify curtain placement and tweak angle (≈ –7° to +4°), width, tilt, and rotation to optimize coverage—especially useful on wide bi-parting lobbies with strong stack-effect or glossy floors.

Activation that opens when you want—only when you want. The microwave channel offers ten sensitivity levels so you can tailor open behavior to approach speed and traffic vectors. Set it to ignore receding traffic to cut unnecessary cycles, hold conditioned air, and protect revolving energy budgets. This tunable behavior is why bea ixio-dt1 shows up in sustainability-minded specifications without sacrificing throughput or user comfort.

Commissioning designed for real service windows. The on-sensor LCD menu and remote programming reduce setup friction: adjust microwave/IR parameters, confirm test input wiring, and run functional checks in minutes. Because the unit is internally monitored and supports external monitoring by the door controller, every cycle can be supervised—a best practice echoed in modern standards frameworks. The result is predictable, auditable door behavior that aligns with ANSI/BHMA A156.10 practices and EN 16005 methodology when paired with compliant safety devices and documented commissioning.

Engineered for harsh, high-traffic environments. Rated –13 to 131 °F (LCD operational 14–131 °F), up to 95% RH non-condensing, and IP54, IXIO-DT1 keeps working in busy vestibules, salt-air exteriors, and draft-prone galleries. The 6’6″–11’6″ mounting range covers standard headers

Easy Retrofit: The Flatscan Retrofit Kit installs quickly on existing headers, making it ideal for maintenance and upgrades.
Weather Resistant: Rated for reliable performance in various environmental conditions.
Note: This kit includes the left and right modules, hub, and necessary cabling for a complete installation. Professional installation is recommended to ensure ANSI 156.10 compliance.

column2: also called ECDrive Roller, Roller suitable for Geze, Roller GEZE EC Drive, or Geze EC Drive Roller in trade catalogs .

column1: Construction: Low-noise polymer running tire bonded over a sealed deep-groove ball-bearing hub for quiet operation and reduced rail wear .

Platform context: ECdrive family features a slim header (approx. 100 mm cover height). The ECdrive T2 highlights a double roller carriage and, with GCprofile Therm, supports door leaves up to 140 kg depending on configuration .
Pack formats: Supplied per wheel for economical refurbishments, pairs for one moving leaf, or as complete roller carriage kits when axles/housings are worn.
Use cases: High-traffic commercial entrances in retail, healthcare, transit, hospitality and corporate campuses where acoustic comfort and uptime are priorities .

Q1. Will this ECdrive Roller fit my GEZE ECdrive or ECdrive LT?
A. Yes—this is the standard roller suitable for Geze ECdrive platforms. For legacy LT variants, confirm by part number or geometry (roller OD/profile and bore) before ordering .

Q2. Is it also correct for ECdrive T2?
A. Many ECdrive T2 operators use the same double roller carriage architecture. Match the wheel profile and size to your installed T2 carriage to confirm fit .

Q3. How many rollers should I order?
A. One carriage head typically uses two rollers. A single moving leaf uses one carriage (two rollers)
column2: a bi-parting entrance uses two carriages (four rollers). Replace in pairs per leaf to maintain balanced rolling resistance .

column1:
Q4. When should I change rollers only vs. the whole carriage?
A. If the carrier body and axle are sound, rollers-only renewals are fast and economical. If axle play, bent brackets, or cracked housings are present, choose a roller carriage kit (two complete trolleys) to restore geometry .

Q5. What field symptoms indicate worn rollers?
A. Rail chatter, flat-spot thumping, drift out of level, difficulty completing “learn” cycles despite correct belt tension, or increased closing forces typically point to tread or bearing wear rather than controller faults .

Q6. Do new rollers change the door’s certified weight rating?
A. No. Ratings are determined by the operator platform and configuration. Fresh, geometry-correct rollers help the door run within force targets and maintain consistent stop positions under EN 16005 / DIN 18650 commissioning .

Q7. Any tips to reduce callbacks after replacement?
A. Replace both rollers per leaf, re-level the panel, reset end buffers, inspect return pulley bearings and the drive belt, and run the controller’s teach/learn routine so parameters reflect the new friction profile .

Q8. What are the most common cross-reference codes?
A. Technicians frequently reference 117380 / 160341 for roller-only, 117363 for roller carriage (complete trolley), and 12013460 for “roller with bearing suitable for Geze.” Use these as verification aids alongside photographs of your installed carrier .

Bring your automatic entrance back to factory-smooth glide with the GEZE ECdrive Roller, the precision running interface inside every ECdrive carriage head. In daily operation, these wheels suspend the leaf from the header, translate belt motion into linear travel, and keep reveals aligned—quietly and with low friction. When rollers wear flat or bearings dry out, you see telltales: door chatter in quiet lobbies, inconsistent stop positions, and controllers that struggle to finish learn cycles. Replacing rollers restores the friction profile the operator expects so the door starts cleanly, tracks straight, and stops exactly where presence sensors anticipate .

2) Materials and bearing design that survive real buildings
Each Geze EC Drive Roller couples a sealed deep-groove bearing with an engineered polymer running tire. Seals retain lubricant and guard against dust from renovations
column2: polymer treads damp high-frequency vibration users perceive as “noisy doors” while protecting the aluminum rail from scuffing. The result is demonstrably lower acoustic signature in healthcare and hospitality settings and extended track life in high-cycle retail applications .

3) When a wheel fixes the problem—and when it doesn’t
Wheels address rolling friction and roundness. If your header shows axle ovalization, cracked carrier cheeks, or uneven wheel spacing, a roller carriage swap (two complete trolleys) is the right fix. Stock both options—roller-only (117380/160341) for rapid renewals and carriage (117363) for geometry issues—so your technician can solve the problem in one visit .

4) How roller condition ties into safety compliance
Force measurements during commissioning depend on running friction and consistent stop positions. New rollers help your installation stay within the force limits expected under EN 16005 / DIN 18650 when combined with compliant sensors and correct teach-in, protecting users and minimizing liability .

5) Lifecycle economics you can defend
A pair of rollers restores operating quality on a single leaf at a fraction of the cost and downtime of a header swap. Proactively refreshing rollers reduces belt glazing and rail wear, which in turn extends service intervals on more expensive components. For estate managers, standardizing four rollers per bi-parting entrance as a planned maintenance item keeps inventories lean and improves first-time-fix rates across sites .

Q1. Is this the right “Controller for Ecdrive” if my header label reads ECdrive T2?
A. Yes. The GEZE ECdrive Controller Unit is purpose-built for the ECdrive ecosystem, including ECdrive T2. Always match the label on your existing board and the wiring diagram in the header to confirm the exact hardware/firmware variant before ordering .

Q3. What exactly does the teach-in routine calibrate?
A. The controller measures opening width and stop positions, checks encoder direction, characterizes friction/force, and compensates for leaf mass. Proper teach-in is the single best predictor of quiet, repeatable motion and minimal nuisance reversals .

Q4. Will this ECdrive controller work with my existing sensors and locks?
A. Yes. ECdrive platforms provide documented inputs for activation and safety sensors, plus interfaces for mechanical/electrical locks. Verification during commissioning is essential to meet EN 16005/DIN 18650 force and safety requirements .

Q5. Does the controller store a history of faults and usage?
A. Yes. Fault memory and statistical data (e.g., cycle counts) streamline diagnostics and preventive maintenance, cutting time-to-fix and callbacks .

A. Both families use modular control electronics and similar commissioning workflows. ECdrive emphasizes 100 mm low-profile headers and, on T2, leaf loads up to 140 kg

Built for dependable performance in real buildings

ECdrive operators are chosen for slim aesthetics and day-to-day reliability. The controller turns those mechanical advantages into consistent motion by calibrating friction and mass during teach-in, then enforcing acceleration/deceleration ramps and hold-open times tailored to each opening. The result is fewer nuisance reversals, fewer “door stops short” complaints, and predictable stop positions that keep presence sensors and safety edges operating in their intended zones .

On the ECdrive T2 platform, the controller supports door leaves up to 140 kg while maintaining the minimalist 100 mm header — a combination valued in healthcare, hospitality, transport and retail where design and throughput both matter . For portfolio managers, the practical upside is simple: one controller architecture across many openings, with parameters you can standardize and copy as sites are upgraded.

Technicians can commission at the door using the ST-series programme switch or leverage GEZEconnects for Bluetooth parameterization, snapshots and reports. That workflow makes it easy to apply corporate standards (e.g., partial-open percentages, hold-open timeouts), capture before/after evidence for audits, and baseline cycle counts for predictive service .

The controller’s fault memory and statistical data give your team hard evidence rather than guesswork: the last errors thrown, how often they occurred, and the cycle burden since the last service. With that context, technicians replace the right component on the first visit and can prove the outcome with updated logs — exactly what modern facilities expect from a professional maintenance program .
Safety and compliance made repeatable

When commissioned with compliant sensors and edges, ECdrive systems are designed to meet EN 16005 / DIN 18650. Product Name: GEZE Powerdrive PL Processor — the primary GEZE Controller (logic/control board) for Powerdrive PL automatic sliding doors
column2: often described in service inventories as POWERDRIVE CONTROL PANEL, GEZE PL Processor, or Control Unit DCU1 .

column1: System Compatibility: For Powerdrive PL series sliding doors designed for large/heavy leaves (up to ~200 kg per leaf) and wide openings

Typical I/O: Program-switch inputs
Operating Modes: Automatic, Permanent Open, Partial/Half Open, Exit-Only, Off
Compliance Context: When installed with compliant sensors and commissioned by trained personnel, Powerdrive PL systems are intended for EN 16005 / DIN 18650 environments .

Q1. Is this the right “GEZE PL Processor” for my door?
A. If your header label reads Powerdrive PL, this control family is correct. Before ordering, capture photos of the existing board sticker and connectors: DCU1 has generational variants (e.g., DCU1-NT, 2M/RWS) and regional firmware differences that affect compatibility .

Q2. How does “Control Unit DCU1” relate to the Powerdrive PL Processor?
A. DCU1 is GEZE’s control-unit platform used across several sliding-door families
column2: the Powerdrive PL Processor is the DCU1-series control dedicated to the PL operator. Spare-parts lists may mention DCU1/NT/2M naming—always match by the label and connector layout .

Q3. How are parameters set in the field? Do I need a laptop?
A. You can commission entirely with the ST 220 service terminal (on-device display, parameter groups, diagnostics). Where available, myGEZE/GEZEconnects adds PC/Bluetooth commissioning and richer logging—useful for estates and complex sites.

Q4. Which modes will my program switch support?
A. Standard modes include Off, Automatic, Permanent Open, Partial/Half Open, and Exit-Only. Schedulers, airlock logic, or special profiles are enabled via the controller parameters .

Q5. Replacing only the processor will fix erratic motion, right?
A. Not always. The board solves control faults, but erratic motion often traces to mechanical issues (worn carriage wheels, belt tension, damaged end buffers) or sensor alignment. Follow GEZE’s sequence: mechanical checks → sensor verification → parameterization → test .

Q6. Does installing this controller alone make my system EN 16005 compliant?
A. Compliance is a system-level outcome. You need the correct controller, approved activation/safety devices, and validated commissioning &
column2: tests. Treat the processor as a prerequisite—not the whole compliance story .

column1: For facilities that live or die by uptime—airports, hospitals, large-format retail, transit interchanges—the GEZE Powerdrive PL Processor is the reliability anchor behind every smooth opening cycle. The Powerdrive PL platform is engineered for heavy leaves (≈ up to 200 kg) and wide spans, combining robust mechanics with a control architecture built for long duty cycles and repeatable, safe motion . The processor is the brain: it reads the radar and presence inputs, arbitrates safety edges and light curtains, commands the motor ramps, and enforces mode logic so your entrance flows when it must and secures when it should .
What professionals care about—and how this controller delivers

1) Commissioning speed and repeatability.
Frontline teams need predictable workflows: the ST 220 terminal provides menu-driven parameter groups and diagnostics right at the header. For estates and high-volume service orgs, myGEZE/GEZEconnects introduces PC/Bluetooth commissioning, data capture, and parameter templates to make fleets consistent across sites . Faster, more consistent commissioning cuts callbacks and aligns doors with EN 16005/DIN 18650 force/response doctrine .

2) Stable, quiet motion under real-world conditions.
Stack effect, temperature swings, and changing traffic profiles alter effective load. The Powerdrive PL control maps acceleration/deceleration and hold-open behavior so the door tracks cleanly and stops where sensors expect—reducing nuisance reversals and throughput hiccups . When paired with fresh running gear (wheels, belt, buffers), the controller’s ramp logic yields clean starts, accurate stops, and low acoustic signatures in prestige lobbies and clinical corridors .

3) Safety and compliance by design.
Modern entrances are about managed risk, not just motion. With the correct sensors and edges, the PL controller supports commissioning to EN 16005/DIN 18650, including direction-dependent activation zones, presence protection, and safe closing forces. Treat safety verification as part of the job every time you touch parameters .

4) Integration and future-proofing.
The Powerdrive PL platform supports networking via CAN and ties into building systems for status, alarms, and coordinated behavior (e.g., airlocks, vestibules). That matters when you’re integrating access control, alarms, or facility dashboards, and it’s why many spec sheets list CAN and interface points on the PL line .

Symptoms pointing to the controller: erratic mode transitions without sensor faults, non-volatile error codes related to motor relay/logic, corrupted parameter memory, or repeated watchdog resets .
Mechanics that mimic control faults: flat-spotted/worn wheels, sloppy belt tension, mis-set end buffers. Always run the mechanical checklist before condemning the board .
Sensor causes: misaligned presence curtains, saturating radar in wind-prone vestibules, or edge wiring issues

GEZE DCU1 Control Unit for Slimdrive SL NT

If your automatic entrance wears the Slimdrive badge, the GEZE DCU1 is the vital component that determines how the door feels to users—ensuring smooth starts, accurate stops, quiet travel, and reliable daily operation. Upgrading or replacing your geze control board (widely known in the European market as steuerung dcu1) guarantees your entrance remains dependable. Whether you are servicing a GEZE access system or exploring robust sliding door solutions, using genuine OEM parts like the DCU 1 is critical for compliance, safety, and longevity. Explore our complete collection of geze slimdrive sl nt replacement parts to ensure a seamless installation.
Ensure compatibility and verify your component details below before installation. Please match your existing setup with the 161556 (Article number):
Product Name: GEZE Control Unit DCU 1 (DCU1-NT / DCU1-2M-NT)
Role: Central electronic controller for motor/encoder, safety sensors, program modes, diagnostics, and guided teaching/learn cycle.

Compatible Operators: Designed for the geze slimdrive sl nt (70 mm low-profile header) and other models in the SL/SLT/SC ecosystem. Note: FR/escape route versions specifically require the DCU1-2M-NT variant.
Commissioning Tools: ST 220 Display Programme Switch (“Geze SL Control Panel”) and GEZEconnects for wireless setup and monitoring.
Program Modes: Automatic, Permanent Open, Partial/Half Open, Exit-Only, Night/Bank.
Diagnostics: On-board fault memory and statistical data (cycle counts, service intervals) to accelerate troubleshooting.
Safety Context: Engineered to meet EN 16005 / DIN 18650 standards when paired with compliant sensors and hardware.
Power / Interfaces: AC input, 24 V peripherals output, battery input for emergency routines, and bus interfaces for networking integration.

Welcome to our technical support and troubleshooting center. Whether you are searching for the official pdf file manual or need help verifying your geze dcu1 nt wiring diagram, please refer to the following critical installation instructions sourced directly from the GEZE Slimdrive SL product family documentation.
To ensure the safe operation of your automated door system, please follow these guidelines from the standard manual:
Safety Distance Planning: Cables can be cut! Lay cables in such a way that there are no cables near the moving parts. Maintain a safe distance of approx. 200 mm.
Fixing the Guide: Securely fix the cable guide (Component 1) directly onto the mounting track (Component 2).
When utilizing your geze dcu1 nt wiring diagram, pay special attention to the pre-mounting phase and the connection between the transformer and the main control board:
Cable Routing Safety: Make sure that cables are cut to length and routed in such a way that they do not become jammed when the cover is positioned and cannot come into contact with moving components.
Cable Preparation: Cut the three-strand cable (Component 1) to the required length.
Wire Ends Treatment: Strip both ends and attach insulated wire end ferrules to both ends securely.
Plug Attachment: Attach the plug (Component 3) precisely on the controller side (Component 2).
Final Insertion: Insert the plug into the control unit securely.
Critical Precautions: Always note the proper earthing connection! Do not mix up wires!

Commissioning with the geze dcu1 sets acceleration/deceleration ramps, hold-open times, and target positions based on your specific door’s mass and friction. The benefit is a predictable user experience and fewer callbacks for doors stopping short or reopening for no reason.
The DCU 1’s fault memory gives technicians hard data: cycle counts, last errors, and event sequences. Service teams replace the right part the first time, reducing downtime.

With the ST 220 program switch, techs can step through the guided teach sequence at the door. Wireless networking through GEZEconnects ensures you maintain documentation control across multiple sites.

column2: Documentation: Capture nameplates, controller photos, and wiring to confirm your DCU 1 variant and options.
Wiring Verification: Replace the old geze control board, double-checking fuses, earthing, peripheral voltages, and your wiring diagram.

column1: Teach-in: Run the full teaching programme: encoder check, opening width/close position, friction/force and mass calibration.
Safety Proof: Confirm sensor logic, safety edges, and emergency battery behaviour in all modes (Automatic, Permanent Open, Partial Open, Exit-Only, Night/Bank).
Q1. Is DCU 1 the correct control for my geze sl nt / geze dcu setup?

A. Yes. DCU1-NT is the standard control for standard Slimdrive SL NT doors. Installations on escape and rescue routes typically require DCU1-2M-NT because of its redundant logic. Match your header label and verify the 161556 article number before ordering.
Q2. What does the “Geze SL Control Panel” do versus software tools?
A. The ST 220 panel gives a four-line menu for parameter changes, commissioning, and diagnostics at the door. GEZEconnects adds wireless commissioning/monitoring workflows, streamlining maintenance.
Q3. Which operating modes can my staff select day-to-day?
A. Standard Slimdrive modes are Automatic, Permanent Open, Partial/Half Open, Exit-Only, and Night/Bank. Your building policy can lock or schedule these through the controller.
Q4. Does DCU 1 keep a history of errors and usage?
A. Yes. The controller stores fault codes and statistical data to support preventive maintenance and faster root-cause analysis.
Q5. We’re replacing a failed board — what is the minimum commissioning we must perform?

A. After wiring checks, run the teaching/learn programme: encoder test, opening width/close position, friction/force and leaf mass calibration. Then verify safety inputs and each program mode before handover.
Q6. Can the control integrate with building management?
A. Slimdrive platforms can be networked and linked to building automation through documented interfaces and accessories. Scope depends on installed modules and site requirements.
Q7. What are symptoms that point to a control-board issue rather than mechanics?

A. Recurrent, non-mechanical faults such as encoder loss without belt slip, intermittent sensor I/O errors across known-good devices, memory-persistent errors after servicing, or a failure to complete the learn cycle often indicate steuerung dcu1 or wiring concerns. Always verify supply voltages, grounding, and your geze dcu1 nt wiring diagram connections before swapping out the module.

Important Note for Installers: If the above reset steps and diagnostic checks fail to clear fault symptoms—or if cross-verification shows the board is unresponsive—this usually indicates irreversible hardware damage. We highly recommend purchasing a brand-new replacement 161556 part to quickly restore your door's functionality. Professional-Grade German Engineering for Commercial Automatic Door Systems

The Dunkermotoren GR 63x55 represents the gold standard in automatic sliding door motor technology, serving as the primary driving force behind thousands of commercial entrance systems worldwide. Doordynamic brings you this precision-engineered dorma motor that delivers unmatched reliability, exceptional performance, and whisper-quiet operation that modern businesses demand from their automatic door infrastructure.
Module Combination: Motor GR 63x55 30V + Worm Gearbox SG80K + Encoder RE20S
Net Weight: 1.7 kg (motor only) / 2.5 kg (complete assembly with gearbox and encoder)
Bearing Type: Premium ball bearing at output shaft
Is this the correct replacement motor for Dorma ES200 automatic door?

If your current motor label displays GR 63×55 30V or your system documentation specifies these parameters, Dunkermotoren GR63x55 Motor is a direct replacement. The assembly includes the exact SG80K gearbox and RE20S encoder used in original ES200 installations, ensuring perfect compatibility. We recommend checking your motor nameplate or contacting our technical team with your system details for verification.
What's the difference between Dunkermotoren motor and cheaper alternatives?

The Dunkermotoren GR 63x55 from Doordynamic offers superior longevity with 3-5 times longer service life, smoother operation through ultra-low cogging torque technology, and better energy efficiency. The premium ball bearings, Class F insulation, and precision manufacturing result in consistent performance over millions of cycles. While generic motors may cost 30-40% less initially, they typically require replacement every 1-2 years in commercial applications, making genuine Dunkermotoren motor more economical long-term when factoring in replacement costs, labor, and downtime.
Why does my motor say ""Made in China"" when Dunkermotoren is a German company?

Dunkermotoren operates manufacturing facilities in both Germany (Bonndorf) and China (Taicang) to serve global markets efficiently. The China facility produces motors under identical quality standards, ISO certifications, and quality control procedures as their German production. All manufacturing follows the same technical drawings, uses the same grade materials, and undergoes the same testing protocols. The production location is chosen based on logistics and market proximity, not quality considerations.
Can I use a 30V motor if my system operates at 24V?

Voltage specifications must match your controller output exactly. Using a 30V motor on a 24V system will result in approximately 20% reduced torque and speed, potentially causing door malfunction, especially with heavier door panels. The motor may struggle to overcome starting friction and could overheat from drawing excessive current. Doordynamic stocks 24V variants of the GR63x55 motor - contact our technical team to ensure you receive the correct voltage variant for your specific system.

While the motor features plug-and-play connectivity for straightforward installation, Doordynamic recommends professional installation to ensure proper alignment, electrical connections, and system programming. Professional installation ensures correct mounting alignment to prevent premature wear, proper electrical connections to avoid damage to motor or controller, accurate encoder calibration for smooth operation, and optimal parameter programming for your specific door configuration. Professional installation also preserves your warranty coverage and often includes initial system optimization.
How does the motor perform in extreme weather conditions?

The standard GR63x55 operates reliably from -20°C to +60°C, covering most commercial environments. For extreme conditions, specialized variants are available. The motor's robust design includes thermal protection to prevent overheating, sealed bearings that resist moisture ingress, and materials selected for thermal stability. In cold conditions, the motor maintains sufficient starting torque even at -20°C, while in hot environments, the Class F insulation provides substantial thermal margin for continuous operation.
Can this motor be used with door systems other than ES200?

While optimized for ES200 systems, the Dunkermotoren GR 63x55 can potentially work with other automatic door controllers that match its electrical specifications. However, compatibility depends on voltage requirements, control signal compatibility, encoder feedback interpretation, and mounting interface dimensions. Doordynamic recommends consulting our technical team before attempting installation in non-ES200 systems to ensure compatibility and optimal performance.

The motor requires minimal maintenance thanks to its sealed ball bearing design and robust construction. Recommended maintenance includes quarterly visual inspection for unusual wear or damage, annual cleaning of the encoder disc with compressed air, annual lubrication of the gearbox with specified gear oil, and carbon brush inspection every 2,000 hours of operation. This simple maintenance schedule ensures optimal performance throughout the motor's service life and can often extend operational life beyond typical expectations.

At the heart of Dunker's motor assembly lies decades of German engineering expertise. The GR63x55 brushed DC motor combines cutting-edge design principles with robust construction standards, resulting in a powerhouse that consistently outperforms conventional sliding door motors in both longevity and operational efficiency. With its nominal power rating of 100 watts and impressive 3350 RPM speed capability, gr63x55 dunkermotoren effortlessly handles door panels weighing up to 200 kg in single configurations or 160 kg per panel in bi-parting setups. The primary Dunkermotoren GR 63x55 motor unit provides the raw power, while the precision-machined SG80K worm gearbox delivers optimal torque conversion with its carefully calibrated 15:1 gear ratio. The RE20S encoder ensures precise position feedback, enabling smooth acceleration curves and gentle deceleration patterns that protect both the door mechanism and building structure from unnecessary stress.

One of the defining characteristics that sets the dorma motor apart from competitors is its exceptionally low cogging torque design. Cogging torque, the unwanted jerky movement that occurs when permanent magnets interact with the motor's slots, has been virtually eliminated in the GR series through sophisticated engineering. This achievement means your automatic doors operate with the smoothness of high-end elevator systems, creating a premium impression for every visitor. Dunkermotoren's engineering team has spent decades perfecting this technology. Through careful optimization of the motor's physical structure, magnetic material selection, and precise manufacturing tolerances, they've achieved cogging torque levels that minimize mechanical vibrations throughout the entire drive system. This reduction in vibration not only enhances the user experience but also significantly extends the life of connected components such as gearboxes, bearings, and door tracks. The low cogging torque design also contributes to the motor's exceptional energy efficiency. Without the constant fight against magnetic resistance, the GR63x55 requires less power to maintain smooth operation, reducing your facility's energy consumption and operational costs over the motor's extended service life.

What truly distinguishes Dunker's motor from budget alternatives is its exceptional performance envelope. Operating at 30 volts DC, the motor maintains consistent power delivery across varying load conditions, ensuring reliable operation whether your doors experience light pedestrian traffic or continuous heavy commercial use.
Brushed DC Technology: The Smart Choice for Door Automation

While brushless motors receive significant attention in the motor industry, Dunkermotoren's advanced brushed DC technology in the GR63x55 offers distinct advantages for automatic door applications. The brushed design provides exceptional starting torque, crucial for overcoming the static friction of heavy door panels. This high starting torque ensures reliable operation even when doors have accumulated dust, debris, or minor mechanical resistance over time. The simplicity of brushed motor control translates directly into system reliability. Unlike brushless motors that require complex electronic commutation, the Dunkermotoren GR 63x55 operates with straightforward voltage regulation. This simplicity means fewer potential failure points in your control system and easier troubleshooting should service ever be required. When combined with modern incremental encoders, these motors deliver position and speed control that matches or exceeds brushless alternatives at a fraction of the complexity. Furthermore, the carbon brush technology in Dunkermotoren GR63x55 Motors have been refined to deliver exceptional service life. Through the use of premium brush materials and optimized commutator design, typical service intervals extend well beyond 5,000 operational hours in commercial door applications, often reaching 8,000 hours or more with proper maintenance.

Every Dunkermotoren GR 63x55 motor that Doordynamic supplies undergoes rigorous quality control testing before leaving the production facility. The manufacturing process adheres to strict ISO 9001:2015 certification standards, ensuring consistent quality whether produced in the original Bonndorf facility in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, or at Dunkermotoren's state-of-the-art Taicang facility in China. The motor's rugged construction features premium-grade neodymium-free magnetic materials that resist demagnetization even under extreme operating conditions. This design choice not only ensures consistent performance throughout the motor's life but also demonstrates Dunkermotoren's commitment to sustainable manufacturing by avoiding rare earth materials. The integrated ball bearing system at the motor output shaft handles both radial and axial loads with exceptional durability. This robust bearing configuration has been tested to withstand the continuous stress of commercial operation, including the periodic impact loads that occur when doors reach their travel limits. The sealed bearing design prevents contamination from dust and moisture, ensuring consistent performance even in challenging environments. Additionally, the motor's electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) design meets stringent EN 61000-6-2/3 standards, ensuring it won't interfere with sensitive electronic equipment in hospitals, data centers, or modern office buildings. This low electromagnetic interference (EMI) characteristic makes the Dunker motor ideal for installations in medical facilities where electronic interference could affect critical equipment.

column1: Built for the System 20 ecosystem

System 20 was engineered by record as a modular platform for standard linear sliding doors. The mechanical package combines short low-inertia drive belts, acoustically decoupled track sections, ball-bearing idlers, and low-noise plastic rollers to minimize vibration transmission into the building fabric (Record, 2016). The STA 20 Carriage Wheel works in this ecosystem as the runner that supports the door leaf on two points inside each carriage. That geometry distributes load, stabilizes the sash against yaw, and delivers the “quiet, confident” travel associated with modern record sliding door installations (Record, 2016).
What the wheel actually does—and why it matters

Each moving leaf typically rides on two carriage wheels housed within one trolley head. As the STM controller accelerates and decelerates the door via the toothed belt, these wheels convert rotational motion into linear travel while maintaining precise alignment in the header profile (Record, 2016). When wheels develop flat spots, cracked treads, or dry bearings, the controller has to work harder to achieve target speeds and stops, which can lead to nuisance reversals and increased wear elsewhere. Fresh wheels with concentric treads and smooth bearings return the system to its intended friction profile so the door starts cleanly, tracks straight, and stops exactly where sensors and safety edges expect (Record, n.d.-b).
Material choice: quiet and durable

Record pairs a ball-bearing hub with a hard-wearing polymer running surface for each STA 20 wheel. The bearing ensures low rolling resistance and consistent geometry under load, while the polymer tread damps high-frequency vibration and reduces scuffing of the aluminum rail—two reasons System 20 doors are noticeably quieter than older metal-wheeled designs (Record, 2016). In high-traffic venues—retail galleries, transit concourses, hospital corridors—this material stack resists fatigue over long duty cycles and keeps entrances sounding premium even as cycle counts climb (Record, 2016).

If you see STA 20 on the product label or the controller indicates STM 20 / STM 20 DUO/RED, you are in the System 20 family and this Record STA 20 Carriage Wheel matches the intended running gear (Record, n.d.-b). Published System 20 envelopes show generous capacities: up to 1 × 150 kg for single-leaf doors and 2 × 120 kg for bi-parting sets, with reinforced STA 20-200 options for heavier sash weights (Record, 2016). While those limits are governed by the operator, profile, and glazing, the carriage wheels are the contact points that determine actual running friction and alignment. Ensure smooth and silent operation for your automated entrances with our premium dorma track wheels. These Dorma ES200 easy carriages (also known as hang wheels, sliding door trolleys, or door connections) are fixed directly on door panels or door wings to connect to the track rail profile. Whether you are maintaining a retail storefront or a hospital corridor, our high-quality ES200 replacement carriage wheels deliver the durability and precision required to minimize downtime and extend the lifecycle of your automatic doors.
Typically, there are 4 pieces in a standard pack for an ES200 easy system, as each moving wing of the door needs 2 pcs.
● Bi-parting sliding doors or double sliding doors – 4 pcs (left x 2pcs, right x 2pcs)
● Single sliding doors – 2 pcs (left x 1pc, right x 1pc)
Model / Part Name: ES200 easy Carriage Wheel Assembly (Dorma Carrier, Carriage/Hang Wheel).

Why Choose Our Dorma ES200 Easy track wheels?

The Carriage Wheel Assembly is the precision trolley responsible for suspending each door leaf on the track, delivering smooth and quiet travel in demanding commercial environments. In every Dorma ES200 class opening, these carriers do the heavy lifting: they bear the door load, maintain alignment, and provide millimetric height adjustment through an eccentric mechanism to fine-tune clearances and sightlines.

The ES 200 easy has been the backbone of countless storefront entrances for years. Using our precision-machined Dorma ES200 Easy track wheels matched to OEM geometry protects your investment in rails, end stops, and safety peripherals. Furthermore, a properly adjusted carrier helps the operator achieve the monitored forces required by European DIN 18650 and EN 16005 safety frameworks.

Each carrier pairs two primary rollers with an anti-riser guide wheel. The anti-riser prevents uplift under transient loads—such as wind gusts or an off-center push—and it helps maintain correct engagement on entrances with air curtains or pressure-controlled lobbies. The eccentric on the main roller axis offers predictable, repeatable height adjustment.
Q1. Are these ES200 replacement carriage wheels fully compatible with the standard ES 200?
A. Yes. This carrier style is built for ES200 easy family rails and door connections, meaning they are commonly specified for both EASY and standard installations.
Q2. How do I level the door after hanging it on the Carriage Wheel Assembly?

A. Adjust the height/level via the eccentric carrier wheel and set the anti-riser so it clears the rail at all positions, then tighten the lock-nuts. Pro Tip: Before hanging, roll each carrier by hand
column2: any roughness indicates bearing wear, so you should replace instead of reinstalling.

column1: Q3. What does the small middle wheel do?

A. That is the anti-riser guide wheel. Together with the carrier's eccentric wheel, it lets you level the leaf and prevents uplift. After adjustment, the anti-riser should not contact the top track along the travel path to avoid noise and accelerated wear.

column2: >ES200  Easy electric mechanical lock - Pulley with integrated locking and belt tensioning

column1: This locking device is an electric controlled mechanical lock for ES 200  Easy automatic sliding door opener. It combines the functions of pulley, belt tension and lock.
ES200  Easy electric mechanical lock by Sanway Technology is perfectly working on original  ES 200 Easy sliding door.
Product Name: ES200 Easy Electromechanical Locking Device — also referred to as ES200 Easy Electro Mechanical lock, ES200 Easy Electric lock, Dorma ES200  Easy Electric Lock
column2: commonly cross-referenced in parts lists as 4000105 DORMA.

column1: What it does: An electronically controlled mechanical lock integrated inside the ES 200 Easy header, combining (1) the return pulley, (2) belt tensioning, and (3) positive mechanical locking in one compact module.
Fail-secure behavior: Designed to lock when power is off and unlock under controller command during opening cycles.
System Compatibility: Built for DORMA / dormakaba ES 200 Easy and widely used with ES 200 EASY
column2: aligns controller logic and program modes.

column1: Installation location: Fits at the return-pulley side of the ES 200  Easy header
column2: interfaces with the belt path and the operator’s modular mechanics.

column1: Controller integration: Works with ES 200 Easy Basic Module (BM) / Function Module (FM) architecture and standard mode set (Automatic, Partial, Exit-Only, Permanent Open, Night/Bank).
Standards context (operator level): ES 200  Easy platforms are documented to EN 16005 / DIN 18650 with modular components for quick install, commissioning and maintenance.
Special note for escape-route variants: ES 200 Easy-2D doors typically require a lock with status (feedback) contact for monitored safety.
Use cases: Professional upgrade or replacement for commercial dormakaba sliding door installations in retail, healthcare, transport, hospitality and corporate facilities.

Q1. Is this the right lock for my Dorma ES200?
A. Yes. This is the ES200 Easy Electromechanical Locking Device specified for ES 200  Easy headers. It integrates pulley + belt-tension + mechanical locking and is managed by the ES 200 Easy controller during opening/closing cycles

Q2. How is this different from a “DORMA Electro Magnetic Lock” (maglock)?
A. A maglock mounts to the leaf/frame and holds magnetically. The ES200  Easy Electromechanical Locking Device sits inside the header and mechanically blocks the drive via the pulley/tensioner assembly. This yields cleaner sightlines, precise alignment, and less visible hardware on glass doors.

Q3. What happens on power loss?
A. The lock is fail-secure: it remains locked when power is off. Once power and a valid open command are present, the controller releases it and drives the leaf normally.

Q4. Which part number should I quote?
A. Many distributors list this device as 4000105 DORMA. Match by photo/geometry to your header for certainty.

Q5. Do I still need a separate tensioner or pulley?
A. No. This module incorporates the idler/pulley and belt tensioning
column2: it replaces separate components and simplifies service.

column1:
Q6. Will this change my door’s certified weight rating or standards compliance?
A. No. Ratings and compliance are governed by the operator platform and installation. A correct ES200 Easy lock helps maintain secure closing and supports EN 16005 / DIN 18650 commissioning when used with approved sensors and procedures.

Q7. Do escape-route (ES 200 Easy-2D) doors need anything special?
A. Yes. 2D systems typically require a locking device with feedback contact for monitored safety

Q8. Any practical setup tips after installation?
A. After mounting, set belt tension per spec, verify end stops, then run the learn/commissioning routine from the controller. Test lock/unlock in Automatic, Partial, Exit-Only, and Night/Bank modes.

When customers or staff tug on a closed sliding entrance, you want a lock that holds with confidence yet disappears visually. The ES200 Easy Electromechanical Locking Device does exactly that for DORMA / dormakaba ES 200 Easy operators: it locks the drive itself, inside the header, using a mechanical blocking element that’s built into the return pulley and tensioner module. Compared with surface-mounted maglocks, this integrated approach keeps your glass clean, reduces tamper points, and ensures the lock engages on the exact axis of motion—where it’s strongest and quietest.
From a facility manager’s viewpoint, the advantages are practical and immediate:

Cleaner architecture, fewer parts. Because the lock also is the pulley and tensioner, you eliminate separate idlers and standalone tension hardware. Fewer components mean fewer failure modes, faster installs, and shorter service calls.

Fail-secure by design. In a power outage, the door stays locked—a requirement for many retail and healthcare security policies. Once power and a valid command return, the controller releases and drives open without manual intervention.

Predictable commissioning. The ES 200 Easy controller handles the timing of lock release vs. motor start, so stopping points are consistent and Night/Bank schedules behave exactly as programmed—no guesswork with adhesive armatures or misaligned keepers.

Quieter entrances. Integrating the lock within the belt path lets the manufacturer tune belt tension and harmonics inside the header, contributing to the ES 200’s Easy reputation for quiet travel in premium lobbies and clinics.
Standards-ready. Installed as part of an ES 200 Easy system with compliant sensors/edges, the entrance can be commissioned to EN 16005 / DIN 18650 targets

Mechanical lock: a controller-managed mechanism blocks rotation/motion at the pulley when the door must be secured—either on schedule (Night/Bank), on command, or by default when power is off.
Because the lock is controller-managed, your access control system sends a single open command
column2: the controller sequences unlock → drive and monitors position/force as usual. You avoid the “two-box” complexity of wiring an external maglock to release slightly before the operator runs—reducing commissioning time and callbacks.

Commission methodically. After mechanical install, set belt tension, verify end stops, then run the learn routine and test lock behavior in all modes.

Premium dorma es200 easy track wheels Replacement

Bring your automatic entrance back to a factory-smooth glide with our premium dorma es200 easy track wheels. Designed as a precision replacement component, these rollers are trusted by professionals to ensure quiet, reliable operation in high-traffic facilities. Whether stabilizing door speeds, achieving accurate stopping positions, or minimizing corrective maintenance, these load-bearing runners are built to perform. To explore complete drive units and compatible assemblies, visit our master Dorma ES200 Easy category.
Ensure seamless integration by matching these comprehensive part details with your installed system:
Product Category: Dorma ES200 Easy Main Wheels / Rollers
Common Part Codes: DS0650010, DS0650000, DS0650-010, DS0650-000
System Compatibility: Purpose-built for the dormakaba ES 200 Easy operator family. (For other series, check our Dorma ES200 Easy components page).
Operator Weight Context: Designed to reliably carry up to 2 × 100 kg.
Role in the Assembly: Each carrier utilizes two dorma es200 main rollers to carry the door leaf, paired with a separate anti-riser guide wheel.

Replacing worn-out components with our heavy-duty dorma track wheels restores the bearing precision your controller expects. This critical upgrade improves start/stop repeatability and force-limit compliance (EN 16005 / DIN 18650). In practical terms, this means fewer nuisance reversals from presence sensors, cleaner partial-open positioning for energy savings, and quieter operation during off-hours cleaning cycles.
Identify the Carrier Style: Always match the roller geometry (diameter and tread profile). We recommend comparing photographs of the inside header to eliminate ambiguity.
Replace in Pairs: For optimal performance and symmetrical rolling resistance, replace both wheels in a single carrier, or all four for a bi-parting, two-leaf opening.

Re-level with the Eccentric: After installing the new wheels, level the system using the eccentric adjuster. Ensure the anti-riser clears the track along the entire stroke before finally torquing the lock-nuts.
Q1. Are these replacement wheels compatible with all ES 200 Easy operators?

A. Yes, they are purpose-built for the ES 200 Easy ecosystem and widely used across all standard installations. However, always confirm the roller’s diameter and profile against your installed carrier and rail before ordering.
Q2. How many dorma track wheels does one doorway typically use?

A. Each carriage wheel assembly (left or right) contains two dorma es200 main rollers. A single sliding leaf uses one carrier (two rollers), while a bi-parting entrance uses two carriers (four rollers). Replacing them in pairs keeps the rolling resistance perfectly balanced.
Q3. What does the small ""anti-riser"" wheel do, and is it included?

A. The anti-riser is a separate guide wheel positioned inside the carrier to prevent uplift. It is not included with the main rollers. Importantly, after hanging and leveling the door, the anti-riser should not contact the top track anywhere along the stroke.

Every set features precision bearings sealed inside a quiet, durable polymer running tire, ensuring maximum longevity in professional settings like retail malls, healthcare facilities, and transit hubs.
