Q1. What’s the difference between a “Dorma Sliding Door Operator,” an “ES200 Operator,” and the “ES200 MDU / ES200 kit”?
A. The ES200 Operator is the full automatic operator. The ES200 MDU is the pre-assembled core (motor + controller + PSU + backbone). An ES200 kit usually means a bundle configured for rebuilds (e.g., MDU plus running gear), reducing guesswork and install time.

Q2. Will the ES200 mini drive unit work in my existing header?
A. In most like-for-like professional retrofits: yes. ES 200 headers share 100/150 mm formats and the controller uses standardized I/O and DCW bus, so your program switch, sensors, and lock interfaces can typically be retained after verification.

Q3. How does the MDU reduce downtime compared with piecemeal parts?
A. The MDU is industrially prefabricated and tested as a single module, so techs bolt it in, connect a few harnesses, set parameters on the integrated display, run the learn cycle, and hand over — fewer variables, fewer callbacks.

Q4. What capacities can I expect after upgrade?

A. Expect the MDU (BM + motor + PSU + backbone) and, optionally, trolleys, belt, end buffers depending on your chosen package — a pragmatic refresh of high-wear parts in one visit.

Reliable Control with the dormakaba BTS 65 Floor Spring

Engineered for excellence, the Dorma BTS 65 floor spring is an economic and rugged door closer specifically designed for double action doors. Offering a highly shallow design with an installation depth of just 40mm, it guarantees an easy and precise fit into the cement box without extensive floor excavation.
The BTS 65 door closer efficiently handles maximum door weights of up to 100 kg and door widths up to 1100 mm. It provides highly reliable performance through two controlled closing ranges:
• Valve 1: Infinitely variable closing speed sweep from 130° to 0°.
• Valve 2: Increased closing speed between 130° and 20° to ensure secure latching.

Available in versatile sizes—EN 3 and EN 4—this system also comes with an optional single-point mechanical hold-open at 90°, making it an exceptional choice for heavy traffic commercial building entryways.

Is your existing floor hinge losing pressure or leaking? Instead of a full replacement, we carry a complete inventory of Dorma BTS 65 replacement parts. By just replacing the spindle insert, you can adjust the floor clearance easily to suit your specific site conditions. Don't forget to seal it with the dormakaba 2300 sealing compound to prevent moisture penetration.

Premium Quality Door Control Solutions

The Dorma BTS 84 Plus Floor Spring is a premium, double-action concealed floor closer engineered by dormakaba. Specially designed to meet the rigorous demands of toughened glass, aluminum, and timber doors, it combines precision manufacturing with maximum functionality. Featuring an ultra-thin 40mm body, it significantly reduces the floor prep depth required, making your commercial installation simpler and more efficient.
Heavy-Duty Capacity: Engineered to handle door weights up to 120kg without compromising performance.
Maximum Door Width: Easily accommodates broad doors up to 1100mm.
Built-in Pressure Relief Valve: Effectively prevents damage inside the door floor spring body caused by heavy wind conditions or abusive forced closures.
Thermostatic Consistency: Built-in thermostat maintains stable closing speeds against drastic temperature changes, minimizing the need for manual adjustments and future Dorma BTS 84 replacements.

Whether you require single or double-action operations, the Dorma BTS 84 Plus Floor Spring offers universal adaptability. It features two infinitely variable closing speed control valves (130° to 0° and 130° to 20°), and offers a 90° hold-open option. The interchangeable spindle setup allows you to integrate standard hardware alongside various deep floor finishes such as marble and carpet seamlessly.

Perfect for frameless entrance designs, this floor spring works in perfect combination with dormakaba XL patch fittings (such as XL PT10, PT20, and PT30). With environmentally friendly asbestos-free gaskets and a sleek brushed stainless steel finish, you get an aesthetically pleasing and safe mount suitable for 12mm to 15mm tempered glass panels.

The GEZE TS 550 NV is a premium, heavy-duty floor spring specifically engineered for high-traffic environments and exceptionally heavy doors. Designed to seamlessly manage single- and double-action doors up to 1400 mm in leaf width, it reliably supports door weights of up to 300 kg.
Adjustable Closing Force: Variable adjustment between EN 3-6, allowing for precise control depending on door size and environmental pressures.
Versatile Application: Suitable for both right and left-hand single-action and double-action doors without requiring hardware conversion.
Advanced Hydraulic Control: Features an integrated delayed closing mechanism (up to 80°) and a hydraulic latching action that safely accelerates the door just before closing.
Built-in Safety: The integrated mechanical back check protects your door elements and surrounding walls by safely slowing down doors that are thrown open forcefully.
The Ideal GEZE TS 550 NV Replacement Solution

If you are upgrading an older installation or seeking a direct TS 550 NV replacement, this floor spring offers unparalleled durability. Its mechanical hold-open device (80°-165°) and top-accessible adjustment valves mean that once it is installed in concealed floor mounting, all maintenance and speed configurations can be handled quickly from above without removing the unit.

Ensure the longevity and compliance of your facility's heavy doors with an authentic heavy duty floor spring designed to meet rigorous industrial standards. Contact our sales team for bulk pricing or exact dimensional specifications.

Upgrade your door control system with the robust Dormakaba BTS 75 V floor spring (formerly known as Dorma BTS 75 V). Engineered for maximum reliability, this highly adaptable concealed floor closer is the industry standard for both standard and heavy-duty doors.

Designed for universal application, the BTS 75 V floor closer fits DIN-Left, DIN-Right, and double action doors seamlessly. It handles door weights up to 150kg and widths up to 1100mm, providing a constant, temperature-independent closing process thanks to its superior hydraulic efficiency.
Closing Time: Two independently adjustable vales (175° – 15° and 15° – 0°) for optimal adaptation.
Mechanical Backcheck: Integrated backcheck activates at 70° to protect walls and doors from violent opening.
Hold-Open Option: Available with 90° or 105° constant hold-open versions.

Need to increase floor clearance or adapt to carpeted floors? We stock a full range of Dorma BTS 75 V replacement spindles and extensions (up to 50mm). Pair your installation with our universal cover plates (available in brushed stainless steel or brass) and 2300 sealing compound for maximum moisture protection in cement boxes.

column2: >ES200 electric mechanical lock - Pulley with integrated locking and belt tensioning

column1: This locking device is an electric controlled mechanical lock for ES 200 automatic sliding door opener. It combines the functions of pulley, belt tension and lock.
ES200 electric mechanical lock by Sanway Technology is perfectly working on original Dorma ES 200 &
Product Name: ES200 Electromechanical Locking Device — also referred to as ES200 Electro Mechanical lock, ES200 Electric lock, Dorma ES200 Electric Lock
column2: commonly cross-referenced in parts lists as 4000105 DORMA.

column1: What it does: An electronically controlled mechanical lock integrated inside the ES 200 header, combining (1) the return pulley, (2) belt tensioning, and (3) positive mechanical locking in one compact module.
Fail-secure behavior: Designed to lock when power is off and unlock under controller command during opening cycles.
System Compatibility: Built for DORMA / dormakaba ES 200 and widely used with ES 200 EASY
column2: aligns with ES 200 controller logic and program modes.

column1: Installation location: Fits at the return-pulley side of the ES 200 header
column2: interfaces with the belt path and the operator’s modular mechanics.

column1: Controller integration: Works with ES 200 Basic Module (BM) / Function Module (FM) architecture and standard mode set (Automatic, Partial, Exit-Only, Permanent Open, Night/Bank).
Standards context (operator level): ES 200 platforms are documented to EN 16005 / DIN 18650 with modular components for quick install, commissioning and maintenance.
Special note for escape-route variants: ES 200-2D doors typically require a lock with status (feedback) contact for monitored safety.
Use cases: Professional upgrade or replacement for commercial dormakaba sliding door installations in retail, healthcare, transport, hospitality and corporate facilities.

Q1. Is this the right lock for my Dorma ES200?
A. Yes. This is the ES200 Electromechanical Locking Device specified for ES 200 headers. It integrates pulley + belt-tension + mechanical locking and is managed by the ES 200 controller during opening/closing cycles.

Q2. Does it also fit ES 200 EASY?
A. In most projects, yes. ES 200 EASY shares the ES 200 platform architecture
column2: installers routinely pair the same lock family with EASY headers. Confirm your header geometry when ordering.

column1:
Q3. How is this different from a “DORMA Electro Magnetic Lock” (maglock)?
A. A maglock mounts to the leaf/frame and holds magnetically. The ES200 Electromechanical Locking Device sits inside the header and mechanically blocks the drive via the pulley/tensioner assembly. This yields cleaner sightlines, precise alignment, and less visible hardware on glass doors.

Q4. What happens on power loss?
A. The lock is fail-secure: it remains locked when power is off. Once power and a valid open command are present, the controller releases it and drives the leaf normally.

Q5. Which part number should I quote?
A. Many distributors list this device as 4000105 DORMA. Match by photo/geometry to your header for certainty.

Q6. Do I still need a separate tensioner or pulley?
A. No. This module incorporates the idler/pulley and belt tensioning
column2: it replaces separate components and simplifies service.

column1:
Q7. Will this change my door’s certified weight rating or standards compliance?
A. No. Ratings and compliance are governed by the operator platform and installation. A correct ES200 lock helps maintain secure closing and supports EN 16005 / DIN 18650 commissioning when used with approved sensors and procedures.

Q8. Do escape-route (ES 200-2D) doors need anything special?
A. Yes. 2D systems typically require a locking device with feedback contact for monitored safety
column2: confirm with your authority having jurisdiction.

column1:
Q9. Any practical setup tips after installation?
A. After mounting, set belt tension per spec, verify end stops, then run the learn/commissioning routine from the controller. Test lock/unlock in Automatic, Partial, Exit-Only, and Night/Bank modes.

When customers or staff tug on a closed sliding entrance, you want a lock that holds with confidence yet disappears visually. The ES200 Electromechanical Locking Device does exactly that for DORMA / dormakaba ES 200 operators: it locks the drive itself, inside the header, using a mechanical blocking element that’s built into the return pulley and tensioner module. Compared with surface-mounted maglocks, this integrated approach keeps your glass clean, reduces tamper points, and ensures the lock engages on the exact axis of motion—where it’s strongest and quietest.
From a facility manager’s viewpoint, the advantages are practical and immediate:

Cleaner architecture, fewer parts. Because the lock also is the pulley and tensioner, you eliminate separate idlers and standalone tension hardware. Fewer components mean fewer failure modes, faster installs, and shorter service calls.

Fail-secure by design. In a power outage, the door stays locked—a requirement for many retail and healthcare security policies. Once power and a valid command return, the controller releases and drives open without manual intervention.

Predictable commissioning. The ES 200 controller handles the timing of lock release vs. motor start, so stopping points are consistent and Night/Bank schedules behave exactly as programmed—no guesswork with adhesive armatures or misaligned keepers.

Quieter entrances. Integrating the lock within the belt path lets the manufacturer tune belt tension and harmonics inside the header, contributing to the ES 200’s reputation for quiet travel in premium lobbies and clinics.
Standards-ready. Installed as part of an ES 200 system with compliant sensors/edges, the entrance can be commissioned to EN 16005 / DIN 18650 targets
column2: documentation and parts traceability remain within the OEM ecosystem.

column1: Return pulley: routes the toothed belt at the non-motor end of the header for a compact belt path.
Tensioner: sets precise belt preload so acceleration and braking are smooth and slip-free.
Mechanical lock: a controller-managed mechanism blocks rotation/motion at the pulley when the door must be secured—either on schedule (Night/Bank), on command, or by default when power is off.
Because the lock is controller-managed, your access control system sends a single open command
column2: the controller sequences unlock → drive and monitors position/force as usual. You avoid the “two-box” complexity of wiring an external maglock to release slightly before the operator runs—reducing commissioning time and callbacks.

Match by geometry. A quick photo inside the header—showing your current pulley/tension assembly—lets our team confirm fitment in minutes.
Plan your scope. If the belt shows glazing or tooth damage, add a belt replacement to pair with the new lock/tensioner module for best results.
Commission methodically. After mechanical install, set belt tension, verify end stops, then run the learn routine and test lock behavior in all modes.

column3: concealed hardware preserves storefront aesthetics and reduces tamper risk.
controller-timed locking supports pharmacy or Night/Bank schedules with audit-friendly behavior.

column1: Model / Part Name: ES200 / ES200e Carriage Wheel Assembly (also known as Dorma Carrier, ES200 Carriers, Carriage/Hang Wheel). OEM-style reference often listed as 9925518001150.
System Compatibility: Designed for ES 200 operator family
column2: widely used on ES 200 “Standard,” ES 200-2D, and ES 200 EASY/ES200e variants.

column1: Function: Precision trolley that links each sliding door leaf to the ES 200 track rail
column2: the assembly uses two load-bearing rollers plus a smaller anti-riser (anti-jump) guide wheel and provides height/level adjustment via an eccentric wheel.

column1: Quantity per Door: Two carriers per moving leaf (left + right). A bi-parting entrance uses four carriers total.
• ES 200 Standard: up to 1 x 200 kg  or 2 × 160 kg.
Door Types: Compatible with framed aluminum leaves or frameless glass when paired with the appropriate glass clamp between glass and trolley.
Typical Kit: Left and right carriers supplied
column2: standard ES200 sets use 4 pcs for two-leaf doors.

column1: Q1. Is this “Dorma Carrier” fully compatible with ES 200 / ES 200 EASY?
A. Yes. This carrier style is built for ES 200 family rails and door connections and is commonly specified for ES 200, ES 200-2D, and ES 200 EASY installations.
Q2. How many ES200 Carriers do I need per door?
A. Use two per moving leaf (one left, one right). Bi-parting doors therefore require four carriers total.
Q3. What does the small middle wheel do?

A. That is the anti-riser guide wheel. Together with the carrier’s eccentric wheel, it lets you level the leaf and prevents uplift. After adjustment, the anti-riser should not contact the top track along the travel path.
Q4. What door weights does this support?
A. Follow the operator’s certified limits: ES 200 up to 1 x 200 kg or 2 × 160 kg
Q5. I’m hanging frameless glass. Do I need anything else?
A. Yes—use rated glass clamps between each glass leaf and trolley to join the panel to the rail profile.
Q6. How do I level the door after hanging it on the Carriage Wheel Assembly?
A. Adjust height/level via the eccentric carrier wheel and set the anti-riser so it clears the rail at all positions. Then tighten lock-nuts.

The ES200 Carriage Wheel Assembly often called the Dorma Carrier， which is the precision trolley responsible for suspending each door leaf on the ES 200 track and delivering smooth, quiet travel in demanding commercial environments. In every ES 200-class opening, the carriers do the heavy lifting: they bear the door load, maintain alignment with an anti-riser guide wheel, and provide millimetric height adjustment through an eccentric mechanism to fine-tune clearances and sightlines.

Compatibility you can trust. ES 200 is one of the most widely deployed automatic sliding door platforms, supported across standard, escape-route (ES 200-2D), and cost-optimized (ES 200 EASY / ES200e) variants. This carrier assembly is designed for that fitting ES 200 rails and door connections—an important advantage for facility engineers who need predictable spares and short downtime. In practice, that means straightforward hang-and-adjust service calls whether you’re replacing worn rollers in a retail storefront or re-commissioning a hospital corridor entrance after glazing work.

Performance aligned to the operator. The correct Carriage Wheel Assembly is essential for meeting the operator’s certified weight limits and duty cycle. On the ES 200 Standard, the system is validated to 200 kg for a single leaf or 2 × 160 kg for bi-parting configurations—figures that give integrators comfortable headroom for heavier shopfronts or laminated glass. The ES 200-2D escape-route variant typically specifies 1 × 150 kg and 2 × 130 kg
column2: meanwhile, the ES 200 EASY is rated to 2 × 100 kg in a two-leaf layout. Matching carriers to the operator class keeps the rolling resistance low, reduces rail wear, and preserves stop-to-stop travel accuracy—especially important for Partial Open and Night/Bank modes where repeatable positioning is critical.

column1: Dual-roller stability with anti-rise control. Each ES200 Carrier pairs two primary rollers with an anti-rise guide wheel. The anti-riser prevents uplift under transient loads— wind gusts or an off-center push—and it helps maintain correct correct engagement on entrances with air curtains or pressure-controlled lobbies. The eccentric on the main roller axis offers predictable, repeatable height adjustment so you can set reveals, minimize mullion clash, and achieve silent travel along the profile.

Professional fitment guidance. For single-slide openings, hang the moving leaf on two carriers (left and right). For bi-parting entrances, use four carriers total (two per leaf). On frameless installations, rated glass clamps are required to couple each glass panel to its trolley while protecting the glass edge—never fasten directly through glass without the manufacturer’s clamp system. After hanging, level the leaf with the eccentric, set anti-riser clearances so the wheel does not contact the rail anywhere along the stroke, and then torque the lock-nuts. These steps are standard across ES 200 manuals and keep the assembly quiet and low-maintenance over long service intervals.

After hanging, level the leaf with the eccentric, set anti-riser clearances so the wheel does not contact the rail anywhere along the stroke, and then torque the lock-nuts. Restore the smooth operation of your automatic sliding doors with our premium quality Dorma ES200 Limit Stop. Designed specifically for the Dorma ES200 operator system, this mechanical end stopper ensures your door panels stop precisely at the desired open or closed positions, preventing derailment and mechanical damage.
Perfect Compatibility: Engineered as a direct replacement for the original Dorma ES200 stopper, ensuring a hassle-free installation.
Durable Construction: Made from high-strength metal and impact-resistant rubber, this ES200 door buffer absorbs kinetic energy effectively to reduce noise and wear.
Adjustable Positioning: The limit stop can be easily adjusted along the track to set the precise opening width for your specific entrance requirements.
Complete Assembly: Includes the metal bracket, rubber buffer, and fixing screws ready for mounting.
Part Name: Limit Stop / End Stopper / Buffer
Application: Dorma ES200 Automatic Sliding Door Operator
Material: Steel Bracket with Heavy-duty Rubber Buffer

A worn-out or broken limit stop can cause the door panels to slam against the frame or run off the track. Replacing the Dorma ES200 limit stop is a critical maintenance step to ensure passenger safety and prolong the lifespan of the motor and belt system.
Note: This is a high-quality aftermarket replacement part compatible with Dorma systems.

column1: Q1. What exactly is the ES200 Controller (BM), and how does it differ from the FM?

A. The BM is the basic module that handles essential logic, I/O, and parameterization. The FM is an optional function module that adds features such as door status contacts, main/secondary closing-edge protection, pharmacy and airlock modes, and synchronous operation.
Q2. Is this dorma sliding door controller compatible with every Dorma ES200 operator?
A. It is engineered for the ES200 ecosystem with matching wiring philosophy, bus interfaces, and program logic. Always confirm the operator variant before commissioning.
Q3. What programs do I get out of the box?
A. Off, Automatic, Permanent Open, Partial/Half Open, and Exit Only are selectable from the program switch. Night/Bank and related behaviors are configured within the controller.
Q4. What diagnostics and safety interfaces are available?
A. The BM provides error memory with fault codes, DCW® communication for monitored devices, and terminals for light barriers and bistable electromechanical locks.
Q5. Does the BM support a backup battery?
A. There is a battery connection for emergency opening or closing. This is essential for egress and security in pharmacies, banks, and healthcare facilities.
Q6. We operate ESA-series entrances. Is this an esa controller replacement?
A. The ESA family uses controllers with similar modes and bus conventions, but not every ES200 BM is drop-in for ESA. Verify model/part numbers prior to replacement.
Q7. What typical faults does the error memory help identify?
A. Field literature highlights diagnostics for sensor wiring, DCW bus addressing, lock feedback, obstruction reversals, and parameter conflicts.

The ES200 Controller (BM) is the proven microprocessor core behind Dorma's ES200 sliding door platform—a controller architecture specified by integrators who need reliability, straightforward commissioning, and compatibility across a broad portfolio of dormakaba sliding door assets.

Technicians parameterize directly on the controller using the integrated display and push buttons, mirroring ES-series workflows used globally. From opening/closing speeds to hold-open times and partial-open levels, settings are incrementally adjustable.

Q1. Is DCU 1 the correct control for my Slimdrive SL NT?
A. Yes. DCU1-NT is the standard control for Slimdrive SL NT. Installations on escape and rescue routes typically require DCU1-2M-NT because of its redundant/FR logic. Match your header label and wiring diagram to choose the exact variant .

Q2. What does the “Geze SL Control Panel” do versus software tools?
A. The ST 220 panel gives a four-line menu for parameter changes, commissioning and diagnostics at the door. GEZEconnects adds wireless commissioning/monitoring and documentation workflows — helpful for multi-site portfolios .

Q3. Which operating modes can my staff select day-to-day?
A. Standard Slimdrive modes are Automatic, Permanent Open, Partial/Half Open, Exit-Only, and Night/Bank. Your building policy can lock or schedule these through the controller .

Q4. Does DCU 1 keep a history of errors and usage?
A. Yes. The controller stores fault codes and statistical data to support preventive maintenance and faster root-cause analysis .

Q5. We’re replacing a failed board — what is the minimum commissioning we must perform?
A. After wiring checks, run the teaching/learn programme: encoder test, opening width/close position, friction/force and leaf mass calibration. Then verify safety inputs and each program mode before handover .

Q6. Can the control integrate with building management?
A. Slimdrive platforms can be networked and linked to building automation through documented interfaces and accessories. Scope depends on installed modules and site requirements .

Q7. What are symptoms that point to a control-board issue rather than mechanics?
A. Recurrent, non-mechanical faults such as encoder loss without belt slip, intermittent sensor I/O errors across known-good devices, memory-persistent errors after mechanical service, or failure to complete the learn cycle often indicate DCU 1 or wiring concerns. Always verify supply voltages, earth/grounding and bus cabling before swapping modules .

If your automatic entrance wears the Slimdrive badge, the GEZE Control Unit DCU 1 is the part that determines how the door feels to users — the smooth starts, accurate stops, quiet travel, and confidence that it will behave the same way tomorrow as it does today. As the central Geze control board for SlimDrive systems, DCU 1 coordinates motor torque and encoder feedback, interprets safety/activation sensors, provides the ST 220 user interface, and records diagnostic data to keep your doors dependable under real-world loads .
Why facility teams choose DCU 1

Consistent motion, fewer nuisance reversals.
Commissioning with DCU 1 sets acceleration/deceleration ramps, hold-open times, and target positions based on your door’s mass and friction. The benefit is predictable user experience and fewer callbacks for “door stops short” or “door reopens for no reason” — common symptoms when controls aren’t properly taught in .

Diagnostics that cut time-to-fix.
DCU 1’s fault memory and statistics give technicians hard data: cycle counts, last errors, and event sequences. That means service teams replace the right part the first time, reducing downtime and repeat visits .

Commissioning that fits your workflow.
With the Geze SL Control Panel (ST 220), techs can step through the guided teach sequence at the door

Slim profile, premium aesthetics.
The DCU 1 sits within the 70 mm Slimdrive header, allowing minimalist glass façades and retrofits into tight soffits. The low-wear drive and self-cleaning carriage concept keep acoustic signatures low — ideal for healthcare, hospitality, retail, and transit .
Choosing the right variant (reduce risk before ordering)
DCU1-NT — Standard Slimdrive SL NT control for non-escape applications.
DCU1-2M-NT — For escape and rescue routes (FR). Provides redundant logic and wiring provisions required under regional codes.
Tip: Photograph the nameplate and the current controller inside the header to confirm the exact variant and firmware family before ordering .
What professionals want to know — and our straight answers

Will it work with my existing sensors and locks?
Yes, Slimdrive controllers support documented safety edges, presence/light-barrier sensors, and GEZE lock accessories. Verify your wiring plan and any third-party devices during commissioning (GEZE, 2019).

Can I continue to use my program switch?
Yes. Existing ST 220 switches remain the primary Geze SL Control Panel for day-to-day mode selection and parameter access .

How does it impact compliance?
The control provides the logic to meet EN 16005 / DIN 18650 when commissioned with compliant sensors and edges. Your installer must verify forces, sensor fields, and emergency functions during handover .

What if power fails?
With the approved battery module connected, the system performs the configured fail-safe cycle (open/close) to preserve egress and security, then signals the condition for service .

A. If the carrier body and axle are sound, rollers-only renewals are fast and economical. If axle play, bent brackets, or cracked housings are present, choose a roller carriage kit (two complete trolleys) to restore geometry.

Before diving into complex diagnostics, ensuring a proper setup is crucial. Follow these exact steps from the official initial start-up guide to initialize the control unit properly.
Mechanical Checks: Ensure the drive unit is completely installed, earthing is connected, and safety photocells/pulse generators are properly wired.
End Stop Calibration: Slide the door leaves manually to the maximum opening width until they touch the left/right end stops.
Closing Edge Check: When closed, the central stoppers should be adjusted so the door leaves touch the sealing strips (approx. 4 mm gap for frameless glass doors).
Smooth Movement: Manually move the door to check for smooth operation. Inspect the drive belt connection bolts and replace them if necessary.
Set Initial Position: Manually move the door leaves to the half-open position.
Set Switch: Adjust the program switch to the ""Automatic"" position.
Safety Release: Release the EMERGENCY STOP button.
Load Program: Turn on the AC power supply while continuously pressing and holding the ""Select"" button on the control unit until the door begins to move slowly.

Once the program loading is initiated, the system will execute a self-learning cycle. During this cycle, the system disabled safety photocells and radar sensors. It will automatically load the factory base parameters.
Power Failure Operation: 0 = No battery mode / 1 = Australian mode (Open on power failure).

Note: To define a customized partial opening width, set the program switch to ""Permanent Open"", wait for the doors to move slowly to the desired width, and immediately switch to ""Partial Open"". The system will instantly save this exact width.
If the system exhibits abnormal behavior during the learning cycle, refer to the following Dorma ES 200 troubleshooting table to efficiently clear faults.
Wrong motor rotation direction registered upon initial startup. The system requires a slow close to calibrate.

Method 1: Press the ""-"" button on the control unit until the door slowly closes.

Method 2: Turn off the main power, swap the two motor cables, and repeat the Start-Up sequence.
The door was obstructed, or power/signals fluctuated during the calibration phase.
You must restart the entire system reset and self-learning cycle from the beginning. Do not interrupt the door movement while calibrating.
System settings are completely misconfigured or custom parameters are causing erratic behavior.
Factory Reset: Turn on the power while simultaneously pressing and holding the ""Select"" button until the door starts to close at a slow speed.
The controller is unresponsive to regular commands.
Ensure the switch is on ""Automatic"". Press and hold the ""Select"" button for exactly 3 seconds to force a manual learning cycle.

DORMA ED250 Learning Cycle — Executed by ADS2005 Board
The learning cycle is a firmware routine executed by the ed250 ads2005 control board. The board drives the motor through a measurement sequence and stores learned travel/force values in its memory.
• Do NOT move the door leaf manually during the cycle — the board cannot learn correctly if interfered with.
• Safety sensors switched OFF at board terminals during the cycle.
Phase 1 — Learn Required: Display shows small rotating o and O. Action: Press and hold ▼ for 3 seconds to initiate.
Phase 2 — Movement Sequence: Symbols scroll through display. Board drives motor through measurement movements. Action: Do NOT interrupt — let board complete automatically.

column1: What is the correct installation position for the ED100 / ED250 standard arm?

The Dorma ED100 ED250 standard arm described in this manual is mounted on the opposite hinge side of the door leaf — also referred to as the Dorma ED250 push arm or push-version configuration. First fix the arm to the slide channel following the operator-specific sequence, then proceed to the adjustment screw steps below.
How do I install the adjustment screw and arm on the operator axle?
Follow the factory procedure exactly when installing the ED250 standard arm 29271021 or equivalent ED100 arm replacement:
Step 1: Fix the adjustment screw (A) with 2 screws through the provided holes.
Step 2: Use a high torque of 35 Nm to fix the arm (B) to the operator axle.

⚠️ Critical warning: Only use the provided self-locking screw. If the screw has to be relaxed during repair or maintenance work, it must be replaced by a new self-locking screw (see spare part list). Reusing a previously tightened self-locking screw can cause loosening under vibration and unsafe operation.
How do I align the adjustment screw perpendicular to the door leaf?
The adjustment screw must be positioned at right angles to the door leaf when the arm is clipped together. To achieve this:
Step 1: Relax the counter nut at the adjustment screw.
Step 2: Relax or tighten the adjustment screw until it is at right angles to the door leaf when the arm is clipped together.
This 90° alignment is essential for correct preload geometry and prevents premature wear of the ball head and clevis.
How do I secure the ball head of the adjustment screw inside the arm?
After setting the 90° angle, complete the assembly of the Dorma ED100 ED250 standard arm:
Step 1: Press the ball head of the adjustment screw into the provided hole inside the arm.
Step 2: Secure the adjustment screw with the aid of the hexagon nut.

What happens if the adjustment screw is not at right angles to the door leaf?
When the adjustment screw of the ED100 250 XEA standard arm is not perpendicular to the door leaf, the following failures can occur:
• The linkage may bind or click during operation.
• Premature wear develops at the ball head and clevis joints.
• The operator may misread the door position, leading to inconsistent opening/closing angles or fault conditions.
• The door leaf can sag or fail to reach the fully closed position.
If these symptoms persist after correctly aligning the screw and replacing the self-locking screw, the arm itself has exceeded its wear limits.
What symptoms indicate that the standard arm needs replacement?
Common failure signs that point to an ED100 250 arm replacement rather than a repair include:
Clicking or knocking noise from the linkage during each cycle
Sagging or drooping of the door leaf when in the closed position
Excessive play at the ball head, adjustment screw, or clevis pin
Visible deformation or wear at the arm joints
These symptoms are typical in high-traffic commercial entrances. The ED250 standard arm 29271021 (silver push-version) is the direct OEM replacement that resolves them.

Whether you are performing a scheduled Dorma ED100 arm replacement or sourcing a direct-fit Dorma ED250 arm assembly, part 29275021 is the genuine OEM component that keeps your operator running at factory specification — no modification, no compromise.

The same 29275021 slide channel set serves as both the Dorma ED100 arm assembly and the Dorma ED250 arm assembly. The assembly is also compatible with the Dorma ED100 XEA arm configuration and ships with the XEA-type mounting hardware, so no extra bracket is required for XEA-fit doors.

When installing or replacing the Dorma ED100 arm assembly / Dorma ED250 arm assembly, the slide channel on the hinge side uses five indexed components. Knowing each part by name speeds up fault-finding and reordering.
Slide channel — Main guide rail mounted to the door frame hinge side.
End stop — Limits the travel of the slide shoe at the end of the channel.
Buffer — Dampens impact when the slide shoe reaches the end stop.
Slide shoe — Carries the pivot pin and transfers motion between arm and channel.
Fixing — Secures the channel and end caps in position (2 screws provided).
Mounting the Slide Channel on the Hinge Side (ED100 / ED250)

Follow the factory procedure below when fitting the slide channel during an ED100 arm replacement or Dorma ED250 arm replacement. Skipping a step is the most common cause of post-install rattle and poor closing speed.
Step 1 — Assemble the slide shoe: Insert the correct pivot pin into the slide shoe and secure it with the lock washer.
Step 2 — Load the channel: Position all five components inside the slide channel in order: slide channel → end stop → buffer → slide shoe → fixing.
Step 3 — Lock the fixings: Screw down the fixings through the provided holes to lock the assembly inside the channel.
Step 4 — Fix to the frame: Secure the slide channel to the frame with 2 screws through the provided mounting holes.
Step 5 — Fit the cover: Mount the slide channel cover, ensuring the end caps are flush with the cover on both sides after installing the spacers.
Alignment check: Confirm the mounting position is correct before final tightening. The end caps must sit flush with the cover on both sides.
The pivot pin length depends on the door rebate configuration. Using the wrong pin is a frequent cause of premature wear in the Dorma ED100 slide channel and can lead to arm play or noisy operation.
12.5 mm pin: Use for doors with a rebate.
25 mm pin: Use for doors with a deeper rebate / thicker door edge.
Short pin: Use only for doors without a rebate.
Correct fastening is critical for safe operation of the 29275021 ED100 arm assembly.
Torque: Tighten the arm-to-operator-axle bolt to 35 Nm.
Fastener: Use only the provided self-locking screw supplied by Dorma.
Maintenance rule: If the screw is loosened during repair or maintenance, it must be replaced with a new self-locking screw — never reuse the old one.

Before concluding that the Dorma ED100 arm assembly is faulty, run through these manual-based checks. Most ""arm problems"" on the Dorma ED100 and Dorma ED250 operators trace back to installation errors, not the part itself.
Pivot pin length: Confirm the correct pin (12.5 mm, 25 mm, or short pin) for the door rebate type.
Slide shoe condition: Inspect the slide shoe and pivot pin for wear, cracks, or ovalization.
Channel alignment: Verify the slide channel is parallel to the door edge and the end caps are flush with the cover.
Torque on axle bolt: Re-check the arm-to-operator-axle bolt torque is exactly 35 Nm.
Self-locking screw: If the axle screw was removed, replace it with a new self-locking screw
column2: a reused or standard screw can loosen under vibration.
end stop: Make sure the buffer is seated correctly behind the end stop inside the channel.
